unlinkedReferenceClaims.claimText: A common misconception is that this process completely shields vaccine makers.
Vaccines are held to the highest standards of safety and are monitored extensively for adverse effects.
Vaccines undergo rigorous safety evaluations and monitoring processes.
Vaccines are given to large numbers of healthy people, making it easier to detect dangerous side effects.
Thousands of peer-reviewed, high-quality studies have shown that for the overwhelming majority of people, vaccines are safe.
The CDC has systems in place to monitor vaccine safety, including the Vaccine Adverse Effects Reporting System (VAERS).
Congress passed the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act of 1986, which created the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP).
The law requires doctors to report all adverse events occurring within 30 days of vaccination to VAERS.
Injuries that are compensated can be found on the vaccine injury table.
The Vaccine Injury Compensation Program was created to ensure fair and efficient compensation for individuals harmed by vaccines.
The National Academy of Medicine periodically conducts comprehensive reviews of the literature to monitor vaccine safety.
